note: Zero-model control arms (constant, random, static-checklist, keyword-router, domain-compiler) cost nothing. Episode writing and verification used separate provider calls recorded in their own artifacts.

confirmatory_phase.note: the whole confirmatory phase, on openai/gpt-5.4-mini except where stated

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.note: stopped part-way once the cheap writer was shown to be equivalent; the 26 finished episodes became the writer-swap control, so none of this was wasted

episode_verification.note: two independent verifier families over all 108 episode versions

what_the_frontier_model_would_have_cost.basis: the matched dev/hidden/transfer matrices cost $53.58 on Claude Opus 5 and $3.74 on gpt-5.4-mini, a ratio of 14.3
what_the_frontier_model_would_have_cost.consequence: the power analysis that forced the split from 20 to 41 families cost $3.43 to act on; at the frontier price it would have cost about $49 and the underpowered answer would have had to stand

product_corpus_study_full_150.note: nine times the coverage for half the cost, on the product's actual 150-claim intake corpus

lesson: Development and iteration ran on the frontier model for the first phase at $85.05, of which about $49.72 was development iteration that the cheap model could have made. The cheap model was not only 18 to 20 times cheaper per unit of work, it exposed the parser brittleness the frontier model masked and it made the sample-size correction affordable. Every later decision was taken on openai/gpt-5.4-mini.
